relation_to_csc: Secondary threat - occupies causal self-healing framing; CSC must be positioned as control not recommendation

title: FIRE: A Failure-Adaptive Reinforcement Learning Framework for Edge Computing Migrations
authors: Marie Siew; Shikhar Sharma; Zekai Li; Kun Guo; Chao Xu; Tania Lorido-Botran; Tony Q. S. Quek; Carlee Joe-Wong
problem: Rare edge-server failures are under-represented in RL training data for service migration
method: Importance-sampling Q-learning (FIRE-ImRE) plus deep Q and actor-critic variants trained in an edge digital-twin environment; cost model over delay, migration, failure and backup placement
key_result: Lower edge computing cost than vanilla RL and a greedy baseline under failures
limitation: Learned policy; no interventional comparison exposed; no calibrated uncertainty; no abstention; cost is inside the reward not a constraint
relation_to_csc: NOVELTY MATRIX ROW 11 and ROW 15. Closest RL analogue and the strongest argument for baseline B4. Also the digital-twin reference point: FIRE trains inside a persistent twin, CSC builds transient action-conditioned forecasts at decision time

title: Root Cause Analysis for Microservice System based on Causal Inference: How Far Are We?
authors: Luan Pham; Huong Ha; Hongyu Zhang

limitation: Diagnosis only; study not a system
relation_to_csc: NOVELTY MATRIX ROW 13. Directly supports two CSC design choices: topology-informed rather than discovered causal structure, and evaluation on an executing system rather than synthetic traces

relation_to_csc: NOVELTY MATRIX ROW 14. Methodological ancestor of fork-and-replay. Chaos engineering asks what happens if this fault occurs; fork-and-replay asks what would have happened had we responded differently
